newsitem.title: USA: Vermont House Republicans push education plan.
newsitem.headline: Vermont House Republicans push education plan.

text.p: Vermont House Republicans are taking their education funding plan to town meetings this week.
The measure would replace the school portion of local property taxes with a two-percent gross receipts tax on virtually all transactions in the state.
Exempted would be the first $50,000 earned by any business, as well as hospital bills and exports.
The bill represents the first alternative to a Democrat tax plan coming out of the House Ways and Means Committee.

House Minority Leader Walter Freed says Republicans want to be able to go to town meetings and show they are not just throwing up their arms in despair and are thinking about alternatives. The bill's 56 sponsors include 16 Democrats.
